newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 to 3.00 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 to 3.00 lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 2.00 to 3.00 cents per lb lower on Monday, on the heels of a weak performance in London overnight, traders said.

London robusta futures were broadly lower early Monday, despite $30 higher pre-opening expectations. At the midday break, benchmark September stood $20 weaker at $1,755, after ranging from $1,785 to $1,744.

Friday, New York arabica futures rose moderately in thin trading, bolstered by local and speculative short-covering after Thursday's sharp sell-off. September closed up 2.40 cents, to 164.10 cents, after ranging between 165.50 and 160.75 cents. Spot July rose 3.50 cents, to 186.00 cents, while the outer months gained 1.00 to 2.40 cents.
The July/September switch widened to 21.90 cents compared with 20.80 cents at the close on Thursday, while the September/December switch held steady at 13.10 cents.

Technically, traders pegged September support at 160.00 cents, followed by 158.00 and 155.00. On the upside, they said September faced resistance at 165.00-165.50, with the next level seen near 168.00.

CSCE reported after Friday's close that certified coffee inventories rose for the sixth day in a row, increasing by 4,486 60-kg bags as of July 10, to 70,601 bags. An additional 16,989 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
CSCE also reported that out of 11,666 bags graded only 2,520 bags passed exchange approval.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Monday that there is no frost or freeze in sight this week in Brazil's coffee belt, with temperatures remaining above 50 F (10 C).
In other news, Japanese warehouse coffee stocks totalled 72,487 tonnes at the end of May, up 31.18 percent from 55,257 tonnes a year earlier, the Agriculture Ministry said on Monday.

Traders await the monthly Green Coffee Association of New York's stock report for June. They expected the data, due out on Tuesday, July 15 at 1500 EDT, to be little changed. Preliminary forecasts range from a decline of 100,000 bags to a build of 100,000 bags.
In May, GCA reported stocks of green coffee in U.S. warehouses rose by 122,000 bags, to 1,977,000 bags. Stocks in June 1996 fell by 110,000 bags, to 2,161,000 bags.
